newsitem.title: CROATIA: PRESS DIGEST - Croatian weekly - July 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Croatian weekly - July 25.

text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian weekly Tjednik. Reuters has not verifired these stories and does not vauch for their accuracy.

- After the first soccer match between Partizan Belgrade and Croatia Zagreb, Serbian hardline nationalist Matija Beckovic says the match represents "a first-class social event and an authentic wish of Serbs and Croats to return to normal communications and neighbourly relations".

- Croatian church officials and historians play down reports that Vatican hid Nazi-allied Croatian Ustasha gold after World War II. "It's misinformation aimed at compromising Vatican and Croatia," says ambassador to Vatican Ive Livljanic.
- The independent Radio 101's fight for a legitimate broadcasting license continues, as the Radio now has to register with the Court of Commerce, which wants to see the 101's base capital increased.

- A long journey home - after sensational announcements that the return of Croatian refugees to Serb-populated Eastern Slavonia was a matter of weeks, the reality looks different - U.N. administration has so far verified as habitable only 127 houses in the region.
- Four most prominent Serb politicians and members of Croatian parliament did not attend the inaugurating session of Serb National Council in Zagreb.

- When portraying Bosnian Serb president Biljana Plavsic's struggle with hardline Serb nationalists, one must not forget that Plavsic faailed to condemn crimes Serbs committed in Bosnia, including expulsions of Moslems and Croats and destruction of churches and mosques. -- Zagreb Newsroom +385 1 455 7075
